Hi Evelyn / Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete ask on data handling for the Order Form so we can progress legal+finance review. High-level requirements from our side:

- Data residency: Primary in US (us-west), with DR copy in us-east for failover.
- Retention windows: customer content (PII payloads) must be retained no longer than 24 months by default, with the ability to set per-customer retention down to 30 days for regulated cohorts.
- Deletion timelines: for normal account closure, AtlasPay requires irrevocable deletion and a cert within 30 days; for subpoenas/legal holds we need separate retention exceptions.
- Audit evidence: deletion certificate and a record of deletion job run ids.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support per-customer retention windows in the Order Form and provide a sample deletion certification template? Attaching our procurement matrix for reference.

Appreciate quick turnaround — our CFO wants the agreement signed before month-end.

Regards,

Hi Luis — thanks for outlining this. Short answer: yes, we can support per-customer retention windows and provide deletion certification; I want to set expectations on options and timelines so procurement has clear language for the Order Form and SLA.

Two practical approaches we typically bill into the Order Form:
1) Configurable retention windows (Order Form appendix): customer-specified retention period (min 30 days, default 24 months) applied at tenancy level; changes require 7 business days to take effect for active KV caches and stored data.
2) Accelerated deletion add-on: for customers who need certified deletion within a shorter window (30 days or 45 days), we include an accelerated deletion run and a signed deletion certificate. This is usually a priced add-on on the Order Form.

I'll loop in Vivek for technical details on how deletion is executed and timing, and Rishi for proposed legal wording for the certification and carveouts for legal holds.

Next steps: Vivek, can you add a short note on the deletion flow and realistic wall-clock timelines (hot cache vs. archived snapshots)? Rishi, can you draft suggested Order Form language we can share back to Atlas?

Subject: Re: Initial ask — technical deletion flow and timelines

Hi all — technical details below, summarized into three stages: immediate cache eviction, storage purge, and certification.

1) Cache eviction (minutes-hours):
- Token/KV caches are evicted within our runtime within 0-30 minutes of a tenancy-level retention change; for active in-flight sequences we allow graceful completion and eviction post-request.
- For customers using session persistence, session artifacts are removed within 24 hrs by default unless otherwise configured.

2) Storage purge (up to N days depending on tier):
- Primary cold storage (standard): deletion requests trigger an object-delete workflow. Due to our multi-region replication and lifecycle, data is removed from live indexes within 24-72 hours but underlying block reclamation and snapshot compaction can take longer.
- Archived snapshots / backups: our standard backup retention default is 90 days; if AtlasPay requires accelerated purge of backups, we offer a 'backup purge' SLA that guarantees removal from backups within X days (propose 30-45 days depending on retention length).

3) Certification (upon completion):
- Once purge completes, we generate a signed Deletion Certificate with job ids, timestamps, and hash indicators where applicable. Typical lead time to produce certificate after purge success: 2 business days.

Practical timelines to propose in order form:
- Standard workflow: deletion certificate within 45 calendar days of request (covers cache eviction + storage purge + certificate generation).
- Accelerated workflow (paid add-on): deletion certificate within 15 calendar days.
- Legal hold carveout: we will not execute deletion where AtlasPay has provided a legal hold notice; the Order Form should have explicit instructions and procedure for suspension.

I'll attach a short tech appendix to the Order Form describing job ids and log references.

— Vivek
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 09:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form wording — deletion certification + legal hold carveouts

Team — please find proposed Order Form language below (drafted to be reasonably prescriptive but protective):

"Deletion and Certification. Upon customer request for data deletion, Redwood Inference shall: (a) commence data removal actions across runtime caches and storage within one (1) business day; (b) complete deletion from live storage and indexes within thirty (30) calendar days subject to backup and replication windows; and (c) issue a signed Deletion Certificate within fifteen (15) calendar days after completion of deletion. Customer may elect an Accelerated Deletion Add-on guaranteeing completion and certification within fifteen (15) calendar days from request.

Legal Hold. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may provide written notice of a legal hold, in which case Redwood will suspend deletion operations for the affected data until Customer withdraws the legal hold. Redwood will take reasonable steps to isolate and preserve the affected data during the hold.

Backup Purge. For archival backups, deletion will occur in accordance with Redwood's backup retention schedule unless Customer opts into an accelerated backup purge, which will be governed by separate pricing and a maximum purge window of forty-five (45) calendar days."

Comments:
- I tightened Vivek's suggested timelines slightly to offer competitive shelf-language (15 days for certificate is attractive) while calling out backups separately.
- We should avoid absolute guarantees on physical media block reclamation; use wording like 'complete deletion from live storage and indexes' + backup purge window.

Action: Evelyn/Neha — if Atlas pushes for 30-day cert we can offer 30 days as standard and 15 days for paid acceleration. Also confirm whether Atlas wants the 'min retention 30 days' as a constraint we write into the Order Form appendix.

Rishi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Jenna/Luis — appreciate the clarity. Proposed commitments from Redwood below and suggested next steps so we can get the Order Form signed this week: 

Committed standard terms (per Order Form):
- Per-customer retention floor: 30 days (configurable at tenancy level).
- Standard deletion certification: Redwood will provide a signed Deletion Certificate within 30 calendar days of a confirmed deletion request (this will be the standard, no additional fee).
- Backup purge accelerated option: 30 calendar days maximum purge window available as a paid add-on; pricing is attached in the annotated Order Form (see RI_OrderForm_v3_annotated.pdf).
- Legal hold process: as drafted by Rishi; deletion will be suspended on written notice.

Operational notes:
- Timeline mapping: cache eviction within 24 hrs; live storage removal within 72 hrs typical; backup purge per selected option (standard backup retention may be longer unless Atlas selects accelerated purge).
- Deletion Certificate: includes job ids, timestamps, and confirmation of removal from indexes; certificate delivered within 2 business days after purge completes (falls inside the 30-day SLA above).

Next steps:
1) Neha will circulate the annotated Order Form with the 30-day certification clause and pricing for the backup purge add-on.
2) Atlas to confirm internal approvals on the 30-day standard certificate and whether they will opt into the 30-day backup purge add-on.
3) We will route final Order Form to DocuSign once Atlas confirms.

If that looks good I can prepare the DocuSign envelope today.
